import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.CyclicQuotientGenerator
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Quotient

/-!
# Triviality of the reduction gives cyclicity (W5-T4, the last algebraic link of (iii-c2-aff))

`Tangent/CyclicQuotientGenerator.lean` reduces chart triviality to *"the reduction `M ⧸ (ε)·M` is
cyclic"*. This file shows that cyclicity follows from what the geometry actually delivers —
*"the base change of `M` along `A[ε] → A` is **free**"*, i.e. the invertible sheaf is trivial after
restricting along `ε ↦ 0`:

```
Module.Free (R ⧸ I) ((R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M)   ⟹   M ⧸ I·M  is cyclic
```

(`Module.Invertible.quotient_smul_cyclic_of_free_baseChange`, stated for an arbitrary ideal `I`),
and its dual-number instance
`DualNumber.free_of_free_baseChange_eps` — *an invertible `A[ε]`-module whose reduction along
`ε ↦ 0` is free is itself free*.

## Why this is the honest end of the algebraic chain

Clause (iii-c2-aff) says: an `ε`-kernel Picard class is trivial on each thickened affine chart.
"`L` lies in the `ε`-kernel" means precisely that its restriction along `ε ↦ 0` is **trivial** —
and triviality of an invertible module is `Module.Free` (`CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff_free`). So
freeness of the base change is the hypothesis the geometry hands over, and the chain

* freeness of the base change ⟹ cyclicity of `M ⧸ (ε)·M` (**this file**),
* cyclicity ⟹ a generator (`Submodule.exists_sub_smul_mem_of_quotient_cyclic`),
* generator ⟹ `Module.Free A[ε] M` (`DualNumber.free_of_cyclic_mod_eps`),
* freeness ⟹ the chart class is `1` (`CommRing.Pic.eq_one_of_cyclic_mod_eps`),
* chart class `1` ⟹ `CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1` (`Opens.cechPicMap_ι_eq_one_of_cechPicClass_eq_one`)

is complete **at the module level**. What remains of (iii-c2-aff) is therefore *only* the
sheaf-to-module identification: that the chart module of the `ε`-kernel class base-changes to the
chart module of its restriction. That is a statement about `Opens.cechPicClass` commuting with the
`ε ↦ 0` pullback, not about dual numbers or freeness — see worksheet §6.17.

## Implementation notes

Two mathlib facts do the work, and neither was obvious to find:

* `TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I : (R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[R] M ⧸ I • ⊤` — the base change
  along `R → R ⧸ I` **is** the quotient by `I·M`. This is what lets a hypothesis about a tensor
  product be used as a hypothesis about `M ⧸ (ε)·M`.
* `Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv : Module.Free R M ↔ Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] R)` — an
  invertible module is free exactly when it *is* the ring, which is what makes it cyclic
  (`Module.Invertible.cyclic_of_free`): generated by the preimage of `1`.

The scalar bookkeeping at the end is the only fiddly part: the generator produced over `R ⧸ I`
carries an `R ⧸ I`-action, while the conclusion is stated with an `R`-action. They agree by
`Ideal.Quotient.algebraMap_eq` + `algebraMap_smul`, which is the `IsScalarTower` for the quotient
in disguise.

## Main declarations

* `Module.Invertible.cyclic_of_free` — an invertible free module is cyclic.
* `Module.Invertible.quotient_smul_cyclic_of_free_baseChange` — freeness of the base change along
  `R → R ⧸ I` gives cyclicity of `M ⧸ I·M`.
* `DualNumber.free_of_free_baseChange_eps` — the dual-number instance, chaining into
  `free_of_quotient_eps_cyclic`.

Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5 Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020);
`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §6.17.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open TensorProduct TrivSqZeroExt DualNumber

namespace Module.Invertible

variable (S : Type u) [CommRing S] (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N]

/-- **An invertible module that is free is cyclic.** Invertibility plus freeness means `N ≃ₗ S`
(`Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv`), and `S` is generated by `1`, so `N` is generated by the
preimage of `1`.

Stated as the raw "some `y` generates" rather than through `Submodule.IsPrincipal` because that is
the shape `Submodule.exists_sub_smul_mem_of_quotient_cyclic` consumes. -/
theorem cyclic_of_free [Module.Invertible S N] [Module.Free S N] :
    ∃ y : N, ∀ z : N, ∃ r : S, z = r • y := by
  obtain ⟨e⟩ := (Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv (R := S) (M := N)).mp ‹_›
  refine ⟨e.symm 1, fun z => ⟨e z, ?_⟩⟩
  calc z = e.symm (e z) := (e.symm_apply_apply z).symm
    _ = e.symm (e z • (1 : S)) := by rw [smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    _ = e z • e.symm 1 := map_smul _ _ _

end Module.Invertible

namespace Module.Invertible

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
/-- **Freeness of the base change gives cyclicity of the reduction.** For an invertible
`R`-module `M` and an ideal `I`, if `(R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M` is free over `R ⧸ I` then `M ⧸ I·M` is cyclic
as an `R`-module.

This is the step that turns what the geometry supplies — *the sheaf is trivial after restriction*,
i.e. the base change is **free** — into the hypothesis
`Submodule.exists_sub_smul_mem_of_quotient_cyclic` wants.

`TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul` identifies the base change with `M ⧸ I·M`, and
`cyclic_of_free` supplies the generator on the tensor side; the rest is transporting the generator
across that equivalence and reconciling the `R ⧸ I`-action with the `R`-action
(`Ideal.Quotient.algebraMap_eq` + `algebraMap_smul`).

The raised heartbeat budget is for the `TensorProduct`/`Submodule.Quotient` instance towers on
`(R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M`, which are deep; the proof itself is six steps. -/
theorem quotient_smul_cyclic_of_free_baseChange [Module.Invertible R M] (I : Ideal R)
    (hfree : Module.Free (R ⧸ I) ((R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M)) :
    ∃ y : M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)), ∀ z, ∃ r : R, z = r • y := by
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := Module.Invertible.cyclic_of_free (R ⧸ I) ((R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] M)
  set E := TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I with hE
  refine ⟨E y, fun z => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := hy (E.symm z)
  obtain ⟨r', rfl⟩ := Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective r
  refine ⟨r', ?_⟩
  have key : E (E.symm z) = E (Ideal.Quotient.mk I r' • y) := congrArg E hr
  rw [E.apply_symm_apply] at key
  rw [key]
  have hsm : (Ideal.Quotient.mk I r') • y = r' • y := by
    rw [← Ideal.Quotient.algebraMap_eq, algebraMap_smul]
  rw [hsm, E.map_smul]

end Module.Invertible

namespace DualNumber

variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A]

/-- **Chart triviality from freeness of the reduction** — the form clause (iii-c2-aff) hands over.

An invertible `A[ε]`-module whose base change along `ε ↦ 0` is free is itself free. "Free after
restriction" is exactly "the restricted class is trivial in the Picard group"
(`CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff_free`), so this is the module-level statement of *"an `ε`-kernel class
is trivial on the chart"*.

Composite of `Module.Invertible.quotient_smul_cyclic_of_free_baseChange` (freeness of the base
change ⟹ cyclic reduction) with `free_of_quotient_eps_cyclic` (cyclic reduction ⟹ free), the
latter itself the sibling-ported generator step. Note the base change is taken along
`A[ε] ⧸ (ε)`, not along `A` — the two are isomorphic but the statement is phrased on the quotient
so that no ring identification is needed here. -/
theorem free_of_free_baseChange_eps
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (DualNumber A) M]
    [Module.Invertible (DualNumber A) M]
    (hfree : Module.Free (DualNumber A ⧸ Ideal.span {(ε : DualNumber A)})
      ((DualNumber A ⧸ Ideal.span {(ε : DualNumber A)}) ⊗[DualNumber A] M)) :
    Module.Free (DualNumber A) M :=
  free_of_quotient_eps_cyclic A M
    (Module.Invertible.quotient_smul_cyclic_of_free_baseChange
      (Ideal.span {(ε : DualNumber A)}) hfree)

end DualNumber

# AlgebraicJacobian (rebuild)

<!-- archon:readme -->

## Project

A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.

This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.

It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).

  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.
